faqs.question: How much does a website cost?
faqs.answer: Most marketing sites cost between $5k and $50k, depending on the number of pages, integrations and 3D. After a short call we send a fixed quote, so the price never changes without your approval.

faqs.question: How long does a project take?
faqs.answer: A marketing site usually takes 6 to 10 weeks from the first workshop to launch. You get a preview link in the first week and see progress every week after that.

faqs.question: Do you offer support after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every project includes 30 days of free support, and most clients continue with a monthly plan for updates, monitoring and improvements.

faqs.question: Will the 3D work on phones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Scenes adapt to the device: phones get a lighter version, and visitors who prefer reduced motion or save data see a static design instead.

faqs.question: Can we edit the content ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your team edits pages, posts and case studies in a dashboard, and changes go live without a developer.

content.text: What we collect
When you contact us we collect the details you enter in the form: your name, email address, company and message. We also record the IP address of the request to protect the form against abuse.
Why we use it
We use these details only to answer your request and, if you become a client, to deliver our services. We do not sell your data.
Analytics
We use privacy-friendly analytics that do not set cookies or track you across websites.
Security checks
Our forms use Cloudflare Turnstile to tell people and bots apart. Cloudflare processes technical data about your browser for this purpose.
Your rights
You can ask us for a copy of your data or ask us to delete it at any time by writing to
hello@agency.com
Using this website
You may browse this website for personal and business purposes. Do not attempt to disrupt it, probe it for vulnerabilities without permission or submit automated requests.
Content
All content on this website belongs to Agency Ltd. unless stated otherwise. Sample projects are illustrations and not client endorsements.
Projects
Client work is governed by a separate written agreement signed before work starts.
Liability
The website is provided as is. We work hard to keep it accurate and available but cannot guarantee it is free of errors or interruptions.
Contact
Questions about these terms:
hello@agency.com
Our approach
The public website does not use advertising or tracking cookies, so there is no cookie banner. Our analytics are cookieless.
Strictly necessary cookies
Cloudflare may set short-lived security cookies to protect the site and our forms from abuse. The client portal, when it launches, uses secure session cookies that are needed to keep you signed in.
Questions

content.text: The brief
Launch a new pair of headphones with a configurator that lets buyers try every colour and finish, on any device, without a plugin or a slow first load.
What we built
A WebGL scene with physically based materials, compressed with Draco and KTX2.
A configurator state that lives in the URL, so every combination can be shared.
A static fallback image for reduced motion, data saver and devices without WebGL.
How we kept it fast
The 3D chunk loads after the product copy, and the scene drops to a lighter quality tier when the frame rate falls. The page itself is static and served from the CDN.

data.description: Five habits that keep real-time WebGL scenes at 30+ frames per second on the phones most visitors actually own.
data.author: Agency studio

content.text: A 3D hero that stutters is worse than no 3D at all. These are the rules we apply on every scene.
1. Load it last
The scene is a separate chunk that downloads after the page is usable. Visitors read the headline first; the particles arrive a moment later.
2. One draw call where you can
Hundreds of particles share one instanced mesh. Each extra draw call costs time on the CPU, and mobile CPUs have little to spare.
3. Measure, then degrade
We start on a quality tier picked from the device's cores and memory, then drop to a lighter tier when the frame rate falls.
4. Stop when nobody is looking
When the hero scrolls out of view or the tab is hidden, the render loop stops completely.
5. Respect the visitor
With
reduced motion
or
data saver
switched on, we show a static illustration instead. It is the same story, without the cost.

title: Why we prerender every marketing page

data.description: Static pages load faster, cost less and are easier to secure. Here is how we keep a 3D-heavy site static without giving up interactivity.
data.author: Agency studio

content.text: Most marketing pages do not change between two visitors. So we build them once, at deploy time, and serve the same HTML from a CDN close to every reader.
What static buys you
Speed.
The first byte comes from the edge, not from a server that renders on demand.
Resilience.
A traffic spike hits the CDN cache, not the application.
A smaller attack surface.
There is no per-request rendering to exploit.
Interactivity still works
Static does not mean inert. Forms post through Server Actions, the 3D hero loads after the main content, and a strict
Content Security Policy
still applies.
A strict policy for static HTML
Nonce-based policies need a fresh nonce per request, which forces dynamic rendering. Instead, we hash every inline script at build time and send the matching
script-src
hashes for each page.
script-src 'self' 'sha256-…' https://challenges.cloudflare.com
The result: every page stays on the CDN, and the browser refuses to run any script we did not ship. Read more about
how we work

data.description: If every control works with Tab, Enter and Escape, it works for screen readers, switch users and power users too. Here is our checklist.
data.author: Agency studio

content.text: We test every new component with the keyboard before we touch the mouse. It is the fastest way to find the problems that also break screen readers and switch devices.
Our checklist
Every control can be reached with Tab, focus is always visible, and dialogs close with Escape.
Test with real tools
Automated audits catch about a third of the issues. The rest we find by using the page with a screen reader and the keyboard.

data.description: Design real-time 3D scenes and motion systems for websites that need to run smoothly on every device.

content.text: About the role
You will design the 3D scenes and motion language of our client sites, working closely with the engineers who bring them to the browser.
What you will do
Model, texture and light scenes that stay within a strict polygon and texture budget.
Define motion principles that also work with reduced motion switched on.
Prepare assets for the web: Draco compression, KTX2 textures and clean exports.
What we are looking for
A portfolio of real-time 3D work (Blender, Cinema 4D or similar).
Understanding of how file size and draw calls affect performance on phones.
Clear communication in English.

data.description: Build fast, accessible marketing sites and web apps with Next.js, React and WebGL in a small, senior team.

content.text: About the role
You will lead the front end of client projects, from the first prototype to launch, and help shape how the studio builds for the web.
What you will do
Build static-first Next.js sites with strict performance and accessibility budgets.
Pair with designers on motion and 3D, and make it run smoothly on real phones.
Review code, write tests and improve our shared tooling.
What we are looking for
Several years of professional experience with React and TypeScript.
A habit of measuring performance and fixing what the numbers show.
Care for accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) as part of the definition of done.
Nice to have
Experience with Three.js or React Three Fiber.
Experience with design systems.
